newsitem.title: USA: Forecasters see warm-up for U.S. Plains, Midwest.
newsitem.headline: Forecasters see warm-up for U.S. Plains, Midwest.

text.p: The Arctic air that has blasted the U.S. Midwest and central and southern Plains should be replaced by warmer air on Friday, but sub-zero temperatures will persist Thursday in some areas, meteorologists said.
"In the far northwestern regions of the Midwest, temperatures should struggle to get above zero Thursday," said Craig Solberg, forecaster with Weather Trades, Inc.

Temperatures in northwestern Iowa, southern Minnesota and eastern Nebraska on Thursday should be the coldest, but the entire Midwest should see high temperatures that range from 20 to 30 degrees Fahrenheit below normal, Solberg said.

"The central and southern Plains should warm up dramatically tomorrow (Friday), going from sub-zero readings to readings in the teens to low twenties by Sunday," said Fred Gesser, chief forecaster with Weather Express Inc.

Gesser also sees Thursday's readings remaining well below normal. He forecasts low temperatures in the single digits for much of the soft red winter wheat growing area in Indiana and Illinois before more seasonable weather returns by Sunday.
Precipitation over the next 24 hours should be confined to the Great Lakes region, with snowfall accumulation ranging from two to four inches, Solberg said.
